findings.title: Mandatory settlement needs an explicit recovery and binding-failure matrix
findings.observation: The design requires full binding validation before authority open, and promises reference-authoritative settlement when the candidate fails. It does not yet specify a restricted settlement opener or operation path after a restart where only the shadow binding is unavailable. Existing apply_fill is explicitly local authorization, not external confirmed-fill ingestion; its risk and audit calls may reject and roll back. The source does not prove the promised mandatory-obligation path. The design itself identifies this implementation gap.
required_resolution: Classify local pre-match execution authorization separately from durable obligations already confirmed by matching; never treat a rejected local apply_fill as a confirmed external fill.

Specify a restricted, fenced, idempotent settlement/recovery path for shadow-only unavailable, unsupported, mismatch, or drift outcomes; both risk snapshots and audit-after must preserve the same authoritative reference result and known contract.

Separate shadow-only failure from unknown contract/authority/reference/shared-model/runtime-binding failure. Unknown authority must not select reference by default. If trusted authority cannot be established, retain obligations durably and recover using the approved exact reference artifact; do not fabricate successful settlement or release reservations.
Define how candidate failure evidence and frozen-new-risk state survive restart without requiring the failed candidate to reopen the settlement authority.
acceptance: Inject shadow-only failure before and after matching confirmation, during after-state auditing, and on restart. Confirmed unique trades retain exact fees, positions, ledger and reservation changes once; local unconfirmed execution can reject.

With shadow-only failure, cancellation acknowledgement, mandatory fees/fills and query remain available; new risk rejects. Unknown contract or damaged reference binding never receives a successful fallback.
If the implementation cannot provide this classification and recovery, keep it read-only/offline as already required by EBD-010.

findings.title: Admission rollback and independent durable freeze need a crash-safe ordering rule
findings.observation: ROLLBACK_THEN_DURABLY_FREEZE is an outcome requirement, but the design leaves the ordering and recovery protocol unimplemented. Rollback followed by process death before the separate control commit can lose the freeze; even a single writer can process another queued command before closure unless its gate is explicitly latched. No observed runtime bug is claimed because shadow is unimplemented.
required_resolution: Define the admission gate, account/generation scope, financial rollback, correlated failure intent, durable freeze and acknowledgement ordering. The gate must close before the next admission can be selected, while existing obligations stay executable.

Specify crash recovery for every boundary between failed comparison, financial rollback and control commit; restart or takeover cannot reopen new risk merely because the separate freeze record was not committed.
If the control store is unavailable, keep admission failed closed with observable results; never report the freeze as durable from the rolled-back financial transaction.
Retried command IDs preserve the original acceptance/result-unknown protocol; a failure notification is not an accepted reservation.
acceptance: Bounded state enumeration or fault injection at each ordering boundary plus concurrent queued commands proves no accepted admission after the failed comparison until an explicit reviewed unfreeze.
Reopen storage after each crash, reconcile failed-command receipts and reservation absence, and verify pending confirmed settlement still progresses exactly once.
